title: Integrality over an ideal is equivalent to integrality of st over a Rees algebra

standard_prerequisites.name: The Rees algebra A of an ideal as a subring of R[t]
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Defined in the statement at lines 8586-8588 and used throughout the counted proof
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the ring over which the element st is tested for integrality and in which the degree decomposition takes place.

standard_prerequisites.name: Degree decomposition in a graded subring
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the coefficients of a monic relation be replaced by their single relevant homogeneous parts.

core_obligations: Assume st is integral over A, take a monic relation with coefficients in A, and replace each coefficient by its part of the complementary degree, using that A is generated by R plus It (proof lines 8595-8600).
Argue by degree to discard all other homogeneous components, obtaining a relation s^d + sum of a_j'' s^j = 0 with a_j'' in I^{d-j}, which is integrality of s over I (proof lines 8601-8604).
Conversely, from an integrality relation for s over I, form the polynomial with coefficients a_j t^{d-j} in A, which exhibits st as integral over A (proof lines 8607-8612).
proof_roadmap: Descend from a monic relation for st to one for s by isolating the homogeneous part of each coefficient (proof lines 8594-8604).
Ascend back by multiplying the coefficients by the complementary powers of t (proof lines 8606-8613).
difficulty_reason: For a ring map from R to S, an ideal I of R and the subring A of R[t] generated by R plus It, the lemma states that an element s of S is integral over I exactly when st is integral over A (statement lines 8582-8592). The proof does not pass to a Rees-algebra filtration: it takes a monic relation for st with coefficients in A, replaces each coefficient by its homogeneous part of the complementary degree, argues by degree to discard the other components, and reads off integrality of s over I; the converse is the explicit multiplication of coefficients by powers of t (proof lines 8594-8613). Choosing the complementary degree so that the two gradings match is the step carrying the argument. H2.
